o: a very low-resistance path allows excessive current

975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.q: Which device is described? "A one-time device whose element melts on overcurrent"
975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.t: Fuse = single use. Breaker = resettable overload. GFCI = leakage to ground. Relay = remote switching.

975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.t: Fuse = single use. Breaker = resettable overload. GFCI = leakage to ground. Relay = remote switching.

975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.q: Which device is described? "Interrupts the circuit when hot and neutral currents differ by about 5 mA"
975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.t: Fuse = single use. Breaker = resettable overload. GFCI = leakage to ground. Relay = remote switching.

975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.q: Which device is described? "A resettable device that trips on overcurrent"
975f009b-Circuit_Lab_B_Mastery_Test.html.t: Fuse = single use. Breaker = resettable overload. GFCI = leakage to ground. Relay = remote switching.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit measures the rate of energy usage, voltage times current?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Volt = push, Ampere = flow, Ohm = opposition, Watt = rate of energy, Coulomb = charge.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit measures opposition to the transfer of electrons?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Volt = push, Ampere = flow, Ohm = opposition, Watt = rate of energy, Coulomb = charge.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit measures the unit of electric charge?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Volt = push, Ampere = flow, Ohm = opposition, Watt = rate of energy, Coulomb = charge.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit measures the number of electrons passing a point each second (current)?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Volt = push, Ampere = flow, Ohm = opposition, Watt = rate of energy, Coulomb = charge.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit measures the unit of electric potential, the "push" behind the electrons?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Volt = push, Ampere = flow, Ohm = opposition, Watt = rate of energy, Coulomb = charge.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Which unit is named after Ampere (one of the "Big Three")?
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: The Big Three: Volta (volt), Ampere (amp), Ohm (ohm).

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: If you break a bar magnet in half, you get:
o: Two magnets, each with a north and a south pole
One north-only and one south-only piece
One magnet and one iron bar
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Poles always come in pairs.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Strong heat or a hard impact on a permanent magnet will tend to:
o: Weaken it by scrambling its aligned atoms
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Disordering the aligned spins weakens magnetism.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Outside a magnet, field lines are drawn from:
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Lines run N → S.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: The Earth’s "magnetic north" pole is actually a:
o: North pole of the Earth’s field
South pole of the Earth’s magnetic field
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: A compass north needle is attracted to it.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Magnetism arises mainly from:
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Electric currents and electron magnetic moments.

a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.q: Two north poles brought together will:
a8f23d04-Circuit_Lab_B_Week_1_Mastery_Te.t: Like poles push, different poles pull.
